sentences.text: Appearance:
Shri Ashish Gupta, learned counsel for the applicant.

Shri Kshitij Vyas, learned Panel Lawyer for the respon
 Order
Heard and perused the record.

2. This second bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of bail relating to Crime No.41/2024 registered at Police Station-Dhar, District-Dhar (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 363, 376, 376(3), 366,
342, 506 & 109 of IPC and under Section 3/4 of POCSO Act.
The applicant is in custody since 23.01.2024.
Earlier, vide order dated 21.05.2024 passed in M.Cr.C. No. 18654/2024, first bail application was dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to renew the prayer after two months from the date of order.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case.
Earlier, bail application was dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to renew the prayer after two NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:23339 2 MCRC-34679-2024 months from the date of order.
He further submits that there is no specific allegation against the applicant of committing rape.
The only allegation against the applicant is to help the main accused Kuldeep.
Whereas, the present applicant is a young boy aged about 20 years and the applicant is in jail since 23.01.2024 i.e. more than six months.
Final conclusion of trial will take sufficient long time.
Under these circumstances, counsel prays for grant of bail to the applicant.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned Govt. Advocate for the State has vehemently opposed the prayer but fairly submitted that no specific allegation has been levelled against the applicant and also there is no criminal antecedents of the applicant.

5. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and looking to the facts and circumstances of the case as well as custody period and liberty so granted, I am of the view that it is a case, in which applicant may be released on bail.

Consequently without commenting on the merits of the case, bail application under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.

6. It is directed that the applicant/accused be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for securing his presence before the said Court on all the dates of hearing fixed in this regard during trial.

It is also directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 480(3) of BNSS.
7.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.

However, in NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-IND:23339 3 MCRC-34679-2024 case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.
